id.description: Present on the materialised object. MUST be absent from the create Event payload: zh/models/common-fields.md derives it from the create Event's own event_id (retyped), so a payload-supplied id would be a second, forgeable truth.

actor_kind.description: Closed Actor classification. agent is reserved exclusively for a controller-provisioned Agent; Applet-created or Applet-hosted automation uses bot; Ghost Actor is provenance rather than an actor_kind and uses integration for an external account/integration mirror or bot for an external bot mirror. MUST NOT include device: a device is an endpoint rather than an Actor principal. actor_kind alone grants no authority; authorization still requires the normative DID, provisioning/registration, Grant and Constraint evidence. See zh/models/actor.md.

handle.description: Arkret canonical handle string: <localpart>:<domain>. The @ mention sigil is not part of the handle.

agent_slug.description: Projection hint for a controller-scoped selector slug backed by ak.schema.agent_selector_claim.v1. Only valid when actor_kind=agent under ak.profile.agent_provisioning.v1; it is not a global handle and MUST NOT be used for authorization, attribution, or Directory discovery. The mention input token @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug> resolves to this actor's principal_id before persistence only after selector claim validation.

resolution.description: Read-only current principal did projection derived from the PCR identity resolution typed current result. It is not writable through Actor Profile create/update patches and is not an authorization root.

actor_profile_definition.description: The author-editable Actor Profile definition: the identity binding the create Event declares and the display members its owner maintains, and nothing else. It is deliberately NOT actor-profile.schema.json. A materialized object schema used as an authoring input hands the author the schema identifier, the Realm binding, the creation timestamp and the most-recent-update metadata, and those members are then retained verbatim by every later write, so a self-reported Realm or creation time becomes permanent truth. They now come from the registered create-lock derivations of zh/models/common-fields.md section 3.3. principal_id and actor_kind stay author input because no derivation can produce them -- the create Event declares which principal the profile is for -- but they are create-locked: zh/discovery/profiles-presence.md section 2.3 pins principal_id to the submitter or an explicitly authorized target at create, and rebinding a profile to another principal, or retyping a user as an agent, is a new object rather than a patch. id and resolution stay out for the reasons actor_profile_create_payload already gave, and status is gone from the durable object entirely: it projected an AccountStatusRecord, which zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md section 3 keeps out of every reducer.
